title: C1751 — Daytime Running Lamp (DRL), RF
introduction:
This reference maps the right-front daytime running lamp connector. I start with CNumber and Description, then use the cavity labels in the drawing to find the matching assignment rows. Think of a cavity label as the street address and the circuit entry as the name on the mailbox: the shape helps you navigate, but the row tells you what the connection serves.

Read across a row to keep its circuit, color, gauge, function and terminal information together. The ground entry describes the current's return path; the control-module entry identifies the lamp's control connection. The part-information table beneath the drawing provides a separate connector reference. Gauge conventions and the meanings of Box, Cols, Size and Used are not explained, and a blank Qualifier cell adds no configuration guidance. This sheet supplies no access steps, physical viewing-side designation, test values or replacement procedure; use it to understand the map before moving to the applicable service instructions.

edits.why: In the drawing as printed, the upper cavity corresponds to the ground entry and the lower cavity to the control-module entry. That describes their positions on the page; it does not establish which side of the physical connector you would be viewing.

Use Cavity to connect the drawing to a row, then read horizontally through the remaining columns. The ground and control functions identify different electrical roles, but neither provides an expected voltage, switching pattern or pass/fail result.
